races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden

runners_data.name: Cyclone Code
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with only two runs at longer trips (6f-8f) on Good; dropping to 5f is an unknown stamina-in-reverse question and 63 days off adds a fitness query, though Simon Cavanagh's patient approach suits late-running tactics if the leaders combust.

runners_data.name: Bit Of A Buzz
runners_data.note: Most experienced front-runner in the field with six starts and three placed efforts at 5f on Good-ish ground; Gavin Cromwell's stable is in form (T14: 5/41) and Gary Carroll is a strong booking, making this the most credible pace-setter to sustain its effort if rivals over-commit early.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Dream
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning just 10 days after a race, but both form runs came at 6f-7f and on Soft or Standard; the drop to 5f on Good is a significant profile mismatch and its record shows no placings, raising doubts about whether it will last in a contested lead.

runners_data.name: Gus Mccrae
runners_data.note: Unexposed debutant whose stable profile (Noel Meade) and jockey assignment (Colin Keane) both represent elite connections for a maiden; style and going entirely unknown but the talent pedigree demands respect in a field where the pace scenario suits a fresh, well-prepared runner.

runners_data.name: Ahorey
runners_data.note: Another debut runner with no form to assess, but Seamie Heffernan's presence is a significant live jockey flag; W R Crawford has only five runners in the 14-day window but each booking counts, and this horse could benefit enormously from a fast early pace if possessing natural finishing speed.

runners_data.name: Lion Of Fortune
runners_data.note: Front-runner tagged with a fade flag, which is a significant red flag in a race where pace is already fiercely contested; finished eleventh on sole start at 6f on Good, and dropping in trip does not obviously solve the stamina concern given rivals will push it hard from the start.

runners_data.name: Best Love
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent 5f form on Good ground and a place finish in that context; Declan McDonogh is an astute tactical rider who will position this runner perfectly just off the expected pace battle, making it a serious player if the front-runners collapse at the right moment.

runners_data.name: Lady Romagna
runners_data.note: Debutant for W McCreery, whose stable is active (T14: 5/13); Leigh Roche takes the ride with no style or going data available, so this runner is a complete unknown, though any newcomer in a pace-dominated race could find the scenario plays perfectly if she has natural racing speed.

runners_data.name: Annie Batt
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a placed finish at exactly 5f on Good in her most recent start, which is directly relevant form; Andrew Slattery trains and rides, which is an unusual combination, and 53 days off means fitness must be taken on trust, but the profile fits the expected race shape well.

runners_data.name: Sadie Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner tagged with a fade flag and both runs have ended in double-figure finishes (12th, 14th) at 6f; returning after 10 days with headgear (t) tried last time without success, and there is little in the form to suggest she can reverse that trend even in a scenario that suits off-pace runners.

runners_data.name: Somethingaboutlove
runners_data.note: Debutant for C W J Farrell with Rory Cleary riding; minimal stable strike-rate signals (T14: 0/2) and no form data means this runner enters as a complete unknown quantity, though like all debutants here it cannot be entirely dismissed if possessing natural ability suited to this sharp 5f test.

races.paceDynamic: Scarlet Dream, Lion Of Fortune, and Bit Of A Buzz are all confirmed front-runners over this 5f on Good turf at Navan, guaranteeing an aggressive pace from the break with no horse able to dictate unchallenged. These three will burn early energy disputing the lead, compressing the race from the front and likely setting a strong, even frantic gallop across the first two furlongs. As the pace combusts among the leaders, the race is likely to play into the hands of those able to settle off the speed and produce a sustained late run — the hold-up and prominent profiles of Annie Batt, Cyclone Code, and Best Love are all positioned to capitalise. This race shape firmly favours hold-up and midfield runners who can track the carnage and pounce once the front-runners tie each other up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Burn Out
scenarios.trigger: If Scarlet Dream, Lion Of Fortune, and Bit Of A Buzz fight for lead and set an unsustainable gallop, draining each other before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace will see all three leaders fade dramatically in the closing stages, leaving the race wide open for those who tracked off the speed. Hold-up types who can finish strongly on Good ground at this trip will sweep through, rewarding those ridden patiently from the outset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of Scarlet Dream, Lion Of Fortune, or Bit Of A Buzz out-breaks the others and secures a solo, uncontested lead with a cushion.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner able to control fractions without being pressured immediately turns this from a burn-up into a test of solo stamina, changing the race shape entirely. Bit Of A Buzz has the most consistent front-running form and three placed efforts at this trip on similar ground, giving it the best chance among the pace-setters to hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutants Steal The Show
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the unexposed debutants — Gus Mccrae, Ahorey, Lady Romagna, or Somethingaboutlove — arrives with untapped ability and runs a race beyond their unknown form.
scenarios.body: With four runners making their debut, any one of these could carry a big engine that raw form figures cannot reveal, particularly in a scenario where the pace falls apart and fresh legs matter. Colin Keane on Gus Mccrae and Seamie Heffernan on Ahorey represent the strongest jockey-talent signals among the newcomers, and either could exploit a burning pace on debut.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves strong but not catastrophic, allowing a prominent-tracking type to sit just behind the leaders and sprint clear in the final furlong before hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: Best Love has consistent form at this exact trip and course-comparable distances on Good ground, sitting in a prominent position able to pivot off either a collapse or a genuine finishing kick. In a scenario where the pace is fierce but not race-ruinous, a horse with a prime tactical position just off the leaders collects the prize.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Bit Of A Buzz, Scarlet Dream, or Lion Of Fortune breaks fastest — whichever secures a clear lead unchallenged in the first furlong fundamentally changes the race shape from a burn-up to a potential front-runner's race.
Lion Of Fortune is tagged as a fader and a front-runner in a three-way pace battle; if it cuts across rivals or causes interference in the early stages, it presents a serious risk to those around it.

Colin Keane on Gus Mccrae and Seamie Heffernan on Ahorey are both elite riders on debutants — monitor in the betting market for any late support that would signal stable confidence and elevate their scenario probability significantly.

Annie Batt is trained and ridden by the same person (Andrew Slattery) and has 53 days between runs; watch for any signs of sluggishness leaving the stalls that would prevent her from finding the position needed to exploit the expected late pace collapse.

Sadie Rose runs with a tongue-tie after two poor efforts; if the headgear produces any notable early improvement in position, it could be a market mover worth tracking live, though the raw form strongly suggests she remains vulnerable even in a pace-favoured scenario.

races.name: Navan Racecourse Handicap

runners_data.name: Prairie Girl
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid 5f Good-ground form (three of last five starts at the trip on similar going); Terry Casey's 7lb claim is useful at the weights and Daniel James Murphy has a live runner in this yard's purple patch (1/7 T14); headgear noted (hg:p) and 24 days since last run is a straightforward prep.

runners_data.name: Amerilis
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner, handled Good going well with two wins and a place in last five on similar conditions; W J Lee takes over and Gillian Scott's yard is 0/3 in the T14 window, but the tactical advantage of an uncontested lead in this field outweighs trainer form; tongue-strap and 19 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse for Patrick McKenna who has shown ability on 5f Good ground (five of last five runs at this trip); Luke McAteer partners for a yard yet to score in T14 window, and with eight starts on similar going returning only modest hit-rate (8/15, 0W2P), needs things to go right from the rear.

runners_data.name: Bad Boy Rizz
runners_data.note: Colin Keane picks up this Ross O'Sullivan-trained 3yo whose best form (two wins, three places from ten runs) has come on Soft or Good; 42 days since last run could mean a need for the outing, but the talent is there and a prominent-to-midfield position could see him involved late on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has won twice and placed five times from fifteen runs on similar going; Siobhan Rutledge's claim helps at OR 76 and the horse returns just six days after its last start — the quick turnaround is notable and the yard (0/4 T14) offers no trainer confidence, but the horse's Good-ground record is respectable.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: Jessica O'Gorman (7lb claimer) takes the ride for Daniel James Murphy, who has a 1/7 T14 strike rate suggesting the yard is in form; hold-up style at a track where a single modest pace-setter is unlikely to create the gaps this horse needs, and a mixed recent record (1W1P from 11 similar-going starts) limits expectations.

runners_data.name: Dandyville
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old returning after 18 days whose recent form reads 7000-0 — consistently well beaten in recent outings; history on Good going shows occasional placing (0W2P from 15 runs) but this is a horse well down the handicap ladder now and a hold-up style in a non-pace scenario is a structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Shadow Of The Moon
runners_data.note: Goes in headgear (hg:t) and has a win and two places from seven Good-going starts; returning from 66 days off and flagged as prone to fading — a horse whose natural instinct is to come from off the pace but who in this crowded field will be forced to sit closer to midfield than usual, which dilutes the finishing kick that is its main weapon.

runners_data.name: Buddy Batt
runners_data.note: Five-year-old without headgear whose best run on similar going produced a win from 5f on Soft/AW surfaces; 66 days off the track is the longest absence in the field, and although a natural hold-up type, the volume of similar runners in this race means Rory Cleary will likely find the horse racing in a box midfield rather than in open space at the rear.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who thrives on 5f Good ground — two wins and three places from thirteen starts at the trip, all on similar going — and returns 17 days after last run with Paddy Harnett's 3lb claim; the tongue-strap (hg:t) is retained, the profile is well-suited to tracking Amerilis, and the course form is genuine.

runners_data.name: Mint Man
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes takes a horse whose last six outings show a wide range — a 19th-place finish last time followed by a win and a place in the run before; naturally a hold-up type but with so many runners carrying the same profile, the horse is structurally pushed towards midfield and its Good-ground record (2W5P from 15 runs) is achieved from deeper positions this scenario may not provide.

runners_data.name: Bold Optimist
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this six-year-old who has placed three times in the last five runs (3/5f/GOO, 2/5f/GOO form in history) and wears blinkers (hg:b); Good-going form is solid (1W4P from 12 runs on similar surface) but the horse's instinct to race from the rear is compromised in a field saturated with the same profile, and the T14 yard stat (1/16) is modest.

runners_data.name: Treasured Royal
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll takes over for Gavin Cromwell whose yard is active in T14 (5/41) even if not firing at its best; the tongue-strap (hg:t) is worn by this 3yo who reached the frame four times in recent outings but whose hold-up style in a field of similar runners means the horse is likely racing forward of its preferred position, limiting the late run it needs.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: Leigh Roche rides a five-year-old with a respectable Good-ground record (2W5P from 15 starts on similar going) and a win three runs ago; no headgear and no T14 W McCreery strike to note, but the horse's natural style pushing it to the rear in a field where rear positions are oversubscribed means only a perfect split on the wide outside unlocks the form.

runners_data.name: Beach Barbie
runners_data.note: Edward Lynam-trained four-year-old with all form on Artificial/Stanway surfaces (four of four career runs on AW); James Ryan takes the ride and the switch to Good turf is an unknown quantity — no Good-going data exists for this horse, making assessment speculative, and a hold-up style compounds the challenge in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Gonna Be Golden
runners_data.note: Robert Whearty rides this A Oliver-trained 3yo who wears a tongue-strap (hg:t); the horse holds prominent placement and has placed at 5f on Good ground before, though the yard is 0/14 in T14 which is a significant dampener; an inexperienced 3yo needing to hold a prominent position in an 18-runner sprint against seasoned rivals is a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: K J Condon's 3yo returns 11 days after last run wearing headgear (hg:p) with Reese Holohan (7lb) claiming; the horse has won on 5f Good ground (1W2P from 7 runs on similar going) and showed ability three runs ago, but the hold-up tendencies mean it is among the runners structurally displaced into midfield in this pace-light scenario, limiting its finishing opportunity.

runners_data.name: Alnofoor
runners_data.note: Oldest runner in the field at eight, returning after 82 days — the longest break — for Ms Claire O'Connell; wears a tongue-strap (hg:t) and Andrew Slattery takes the ride, but the Good-going record is blank (0W0P from 5 runs on similar conditions) and the lengthy absence combined with a prominent style that needs an honest pace makes this a speculative proposition.

races.paceDynamic: Amerilis is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner sprint and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the early lead, W J Lee can dictate terms at a sustainable gallop on Good ground — a tempo that will suit those tracking closely rather than those forced to make up ground from the rear. Prairie Girl, Harry's Hill, and Gonna Be Golden are the primary prominent types who will attempt to sit just off the pace, giving them a pivotal position in what shapes as a positionally controlled race. The field carries a substantial volume of hold-up horses — Shadow Of The Moon, Buddy Batt, Mint Man, Bold Optimist, Treasured Royal, Happy Henry, Beach Barbie, and Cashel Blue are all natural hold-up runners who cannot all occupy rear positions in a single-pace 5f sprint, meaning several will be shuffled into midfield against their instincts and see their chance structurally compromised. With one uncontested leader and a manageable gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in the first three to four, as the winning move is most likely to come from the front or just off it — genuine closers will find the pace insufficient to deliver a late surge from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amerilis Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Amerilis dictates from the front and the pace is never seriously pressured, setting a measured gallop into which prominent trackers fire.
scenarios.body: Amerilis controls the tempo throughout the 5f, with Prairie Girl and Harry's Hill the nearest pursuers, and the leader simply finds enough to hold on or is overhauled only by a horse that tracked in second or third; prominent types benefit because they maintain rhythm without burning energy in early positional battles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking in second or third position improves past a tiring Amerilis in the final furlong on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Prairie Girl or Harry's Hill, having conserved energy just off the uncontested pace, times the challenge to nail a weakening leader close home; both have strong recent 5f form on Good ground and their profiles are ideally suited to this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Amerilis sets a faster-than-anticipated pace and ties up in the final 100 yards, leaving a gap for a midfield horse to come through.
scenarios.body: A runner sitting in the middle of the field — Cuban Grey or Bad Boy Rizz — benefits if the front end goes too hard and opens a seam; however, with so many hold-up types structurally displaced into midfield and unable to race in their true role, the chance of a clean late run materialising is materially reduced.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If significant early pace or traffic trouble creates a genuine gap for a back-marker to finish powerfully down the outside.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires multiple factors to align simultaneously — a faster pace than anticipated and clear daylight on the outside — and the horses who would normally benefit (Mint Man, Bold Optimist, Buddy Batt) are compromised by being forced out of their natural hold-up role into midfield, making a true late swoop very unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Amerilis (W J Lee) jumps cleanly from the stalls — if Lee gets a clean break and immediately takes the rail, the horse could be near-impossible to peg back given the absence of any pace rival; watch for an easy lead from the off.

Harry's Hill and Prairie Girl are both seeking the same prominent tracking positions directly behind Amerilis — if both attempt to sit second early, a brief positional dispute in the opening furlong could disrupt their rhythm and the rhythm of anything around them.

The 18-runner field and volume of redistributed hold-up types (Mint Man, Bold Optimist, Buddy Batt, Treasured Royal, Happy Henry) creates a serious traffic-management problem in mid-to-late race; watch for pockets forming two furlongs out that could trap the most naturally talented horses.

Beach Barbie has no turf or Good-going form on record — all career runs have been on Artificial surfaces; if the horse is uncomfortable in the early stages or fails to stride out on turf, it could cause interference for runners on its inside or outside.

runners_data.name: Murat
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with excellent good-ground profile (two wins, five places on good), returns quickly on 12-day turnaround for Peter Lawlor — the most credible pace-setter in the race and dangerous if the gallop is measured enough for him to conserve.

runners_data.name: The Mediator
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for Gordon Elliott, prominent-style racer with strong recent good-ground form (three placings from last three on good); trainer has hit form at 1/40 in 14 days and amateur jockey could be an asset over this trip.

runners_data.name: Whimsy
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from a 124-day break for Anthony McCann — the layoff is the obvious concern, though she has placed on good ground at 16f before; fitness is the key question in a race run at pace.

runners_data.name: Black Heather
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell who has been consistently mid-to-rear in recent runs; trainer is 5/41 in 14 days suggesting some form but this horse tends to find little off the bridle in good-ground handicaps.

runners_data.name: Not Just Any Eagle
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Patrick J Flynn who showed a recent second over 15f on good ground; likely to be caught deep in the field in a 17-runner race with so many others needing to come from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Friary Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer from T M Walsh's stable, consistent placer over 15-16f on good ground, wearing a tongue-tie; has placed five times without winning in similar conditions and will need a clear run from the back of a big field.

runners_data.name: Timurshah
runners_data.note: Four wins on good ground over 16-18f for Aidan Melia, including a hat-trick of good-ground victories — the most compelling stamina profile in the field; likely to race from hold-up position and his form strongly suits this going and trip combination.

runners_data.name: Jerandme
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old veteran who is a genuine hold-up type but has been mapped to midfield given the excess of closers in this field — his best form is over longer trips on good and standard; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers expectations about getting his natural run.

runners_data.name: Sequoiaspirit
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old natural hold-up horse whose best run was a win over 20f on soft; the map places him forward of his true position in this traffic-heavy field, and at 22-24f trips he may find 2m slightly sharp — a 0.93 STYLE_FIT flag is relevant here.

runners_data.name: Day Trader
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a best run of second over 12f on soft; the race shape pushes him forward of his true closing position (STYLE_FIT 0.91), and his recent form of 06-002 on varying surfaces makes him hard to trust in this competitive field.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with 15 runs on good ground and a recent second over 16f — she will press Murat throughout and her willingness to race prominently makes her tactically important, though she has been placed rather than winning at this level.

runners_data.name: Liberated Light
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse for John E & Thomas Kiely whose win came over 16f on good; wearing a tongue-tie and mapped forward of his true position in this crowded field — his 0.94 STYLE_FIT score is the highest redistribution flag in the race, reflecting genuine positional displacement.

runners_data.name: Rich Belief
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and has placed on good ground at 18-20f, suggesting stamina is not an issue; however, pushed forward from his natural rear position by the redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.92) and his trainer has just one runner in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who won over 13f on good ground and placed over 14f — possibly slightly short of the 2m trip on this evidence; mapped to midfield despite being a hold-up type, and his STYLE_FIT of 0.93 reflects a positional mismatch in this shape.

runners_data.name: Cala Gracioneta
runners_data.note: Four-year-old flagged as a horse who fades in finishes, which is a significant concern over 2m; despite placements on good ground over 14-16f, the finish-fade flag and redistribution out of her natural hold-up position (STYLE_FIT 0.92) make this a difficult race for her.

runners_data.name: Young Churchill
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose best effort was a third over 12f on good — the step to 2m looks a significant stretch; redistributed out of his natural hold-up position (STYLE_FIT 0.92) and recent form of -70370 does not inspire confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Slowdownbarney
runners_data.note: Prominent-style racer wearing a tongue-tie and blinkers for Dermot McLoughlin; no wins or places in 15 good-ground runs but he has the profile to secure an early position behind the leaders and could be competitive if the pace proves sustainable.

races.paceDynamic: Murat and Miss Gitana are the two confirmed front-runners in this 17-runner 2m flat handicap at Navan, and with both likely to push forward from the outset, a genuinely contested early gallop is expected rather than a false or dawdling pace. Murat has won twice and placed five times on good ground over similar trips and is the more credible pace-setter, while Miss Gitana has 15 runs on good going and will press him throughout, ensuring the tempo is honest across the full two miles. The large field of 17 on good turf over this stamina trip, with a genuine duel up front, sets up a race that will be run at an even, relentless gallop — conditions that classically suit prominent racers who can travel just off the pace without burning energy fighting for position. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Sequoiaspirit, Jerandme, Day Trader, Liberated Light, Rich Belief, Jurality, Cala Gracioneta, and Young Churchill are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, while Murat, Miss Gitana, and Slowdownbarney are the runners most likely to actually secure their natural positions at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Murat and Miss Gitana set a genuine two-mile gallop and the hold-up horses find themselves further back than ideal in a big field.
scenarios.body: The even pace strings the field out and those travelling just off the front pair — able to stalk the speed without expending energy — hit the final bend in the best shape; the relentless tempo ensures the front duo weaken late enough to allow well-placed prominent horses to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Murat dictates a controlled but not suicidal gallop and Miss Gitana fades before the home turn, leaving him unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Murat's good-ground form is strong — two wins and five places in similar conditions — and Derek O'Connor's amateur jockey partnership for Murat's stable suggests faith in his ability to control the race; if the pace is measured rather than fierce he can conserve enough to grind home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Late Run
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders burn each other off with a genuinely strong pace and the hold-up types, despite being shuffled back in a big field, thread through in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Good ground at Navan over 2m can reward stamina-rich hold-up horses if the pace is truly searching, but the redistribution of so many natural closers means few will actually be racing from their ideal position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Swooper Claims It
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops unevenly with traffic problems in the big field and a progressive mid-division horse picks the right path through late.
scenarios.body: Timurshah's four wins on good ground over 2m trips show genuine course-profile suitability, and a messy-run race in a 17-runner handicap could gift a poised midfield mover a gap that others miss.

watchPoints.text: Timurshah is the standout stamina profile in the field — four wins on good ground over 16-18f — and if he gets a clean passage from his hold-up position in the final quarter-mile, his form suggests he is well-weighted to challenge.

The Murat–Miss Gitana duel for the lead could establish an unsustainably strong gallop over 2m on good ground; any horse caught in the middle of a 17-runner field could find themselves shuffled back and out of contention by the home turn.

Multiple hold-up horses (Sequoiaspirit, Jerandme, Day Trader, Liberated Light, Rich Belief) are all racing forward of their natural positions due to redistribution — watch for congestion and interference in the middle of the field around the final bend.

The Mediator is only four days off his last run for Gordon Elliott, who is 1/40 in the past 14 days — the quick turnaround for an in-form stable runner with strong good-ground recent form is a live angle worth tracking in running.

Friary Road and Timurshah both carry tongue-ties and have placed consistently without always winning — in a race where the pace pressure is genuine, both could be involved late if they avoid traffic, making the final quarter-mile particularly important to watch.

runners_data.name: Storzando

runners_data.name: Emiza

runners_data.name: Pattyandselma
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for Adrian McGuinness with Rory Cleary booked; style and going preference are completely unknown, and the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 3/24 gives some encouragement that the stable sends runners ready, but this is pure speculation without a racecourse run to reference.|

runners_data.name: Riyazanka
runners_data.note: Unraced for J P Murtagh with Ben Coen in the saddle — one of the strongest jockey-trainer pairings on the day and a combination that does not waste a good booking on an underprepared horse; complete unknown on style, but the connection suggests it arrives with genuine winning expectations.|

runners_data.name: The Blonde Lady
runners_data.note: One run on Good ground over 10 furlongs finishing 10th, carrying a fades-in-finish flag; A J Martin sends it back over a shorter trip, but nothing in the debut performance encourages confidence that it can reverse that effort in a more strongly run mile.|

runners_data.name: Whatsin The Stars
runners_data.note: Three runs all resulting in double-figure finishes on Good ground, and the fades-in-finish flag reinforces a pattern of being unable to sustain effort; headgear (p = blinkers) added, which may sharpen early interest, but its record in similar conditions is three failures from three attempts.|

runners_data.name: Wooloongabba
runners_data.note: Three runs returning 13th, 11th, and 13th over Good ground, with a consistent pattern of trailing the field; Siobhan Rutledge rides for John McConnell but the form book offers no grounds for optimism, and a strongly run pace will only exaggerate the tendency to fade that is already well established.|

runners_data.name: Xirivella
runners_data.note: Two runs at 8 furlongs on Good turf showing a 3rd and a 6th, with Noel Meade's tongue-tied prominent racer having placed on debut; Adam Caffrey rides, and the horse's style of racing just off the pace is well suited to what this race will produce — it is a genuine beneficiary of the honest gallop ahead.|

races.paceDynamic: Resurgence, Let's Smash It, and Elusive Path are all confirmed front-runners in a 14-runner maiden over a flat mile at Navan, and with three genuine pace-setters heading to the tape simultaneously, a strong, honest gallop from the outset is virtually certain. Resurgence (OR=120, fresh off 351 days) carries the highest official rating of the confirmed leaders but returns from a lengthy absence under an apprentice, while Let's Smash It has been in consistent action and Elusive Path brings recent solid form at this trip; all three will attempt to establish early, creating a genuine test of stamina rather than a tactical crawl. The field also holds Chapel Lane and Storzando, both natural hold-up types who have been pushed into midfield on the map because there is simply no room at the back — with so much pace committed up front, these two are unlikely to reproduce their best finishing kicks from their compressed positions. With the pace bias firmly forward and stamina at a premium on Good turf, this race shape most strongly favours prominent racers who can travel just off the early leaders and pounce in the straight, rather than pure closers who will find the race run too honestly to reel in the principals late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other off and a horse travelling just off the pace inherits control turning for home.
scenarios.body: Emiza and Xirivella, both prominent runners with recent form at the trip, are ideally placed to track the blazing pace and accelerate past tiring leaders in the final furlong; on Good turf at Navan this is the classic recipe for a prominent-racer victory in an honest-paced maiden.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed pace-setters — most likely Elusive Path or Let's Smash It — is confident enough in their stamina to control the tempo and keeps enough in reserve.
scenarios.body: Despite the multi-pace battle early, one leader manages to rate the pace and dictate terms, holding on as rivals fail to close from behind; Elusive Path's consistent recent form and Colin Keane's experience in managing headstrong types makes this plausible, with Let's Smash It's consistent placed record also qualifying.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If one of the well-bred, unraced runners — Testaverde, Riyazanka, or Pattyandselma — is sufficiently forward-going to settle mid-division and finish powerfully into a weakened field.
scenarios.body: A truly run race over a flat mile on Good turf suits a naturally talented debutant who can travel sweetly and pick off exhausted rivals in the straight; Riyazanka (J P Murtagh, Ben Coen) and Testaverde (Seamie Heffernan, Murphy) have the pedigree angles and jockey bookings that suggest they are ready to make an immediate impact.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses earlier than expected, creating a gap for genuine hold-up horses to storm through in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Chapel Lane and Storzando are the only true closers but are racing out of their natural position having been compressed into midfield by the field's pace bias, making it harder for them to produce a clean sustained run; this scenario requires an unusually complete implosion at the front and is discounted accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Resurgence returns from 351 days off and will be immediately embroiled in a three-way pace battle — watch for signs of greenness or premature stopping as fitness questions combine with an unforgiving race shape.

Emiza and Xirivella are the two named prominent racers with actual placed form, and if either settles cleanly just off the pace war they could hit the line fresh while the front three tire — both are physically dangerous runners in this scenario.

Riyazanka and Testaverde are well-connected debutants with Coen/Murtagh and Heffernan/Murphy in the saddle respectively — watch the market moves at declaration as late confidence money on either would signal a live chance in a race that suits an unknown but talented type.

Chapel Lane and Storzando are both being asked to race in a compressed midfield rather than their natural hold-up positions — watch for both being unable to find a clear run if the field bunches in the straight as hold-up horses try to close on a pace-collapsed front group.

Let's Smash It has never raced at a mile, with all four career runs at 9-10 furlongs — watch whether Donagh O'Connor attempts to rate it or commit immediately, as its stamina at this shorter trip is genuinely untested and its pace role may be self-defeating.

races.name: Navan Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Battle Borne
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who fades in the finish, has a headgear note (hg:p) and returns after 75 days off; poor record on similar going (3 from 15, no wins or places) makes this a tough assignment in a 20-runner field.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with a strong record on good ground (13 from 15, 2 wins, 6 places) and a recent win over this trip; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is a useful aid in a competitive handicap and this horse's profile suits a steady-paced mile.

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with solid recent form including a second over 10f on good ground; handles this going well (8 from 15 runs) and Gavin Ryan is a significant booking, though the step back to 1m from a 10f run is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here and maps as prominent/lead by default; returns from 21 days off for Adrian McGuinness who has been in form (T14: 3/24) and gets an uncontested lead, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reminds us this horse is racing slightly out of its usual role.

runners_data.name: Blue Orquidea
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old hold-up type with only three runs, all on good or soft ground; handles this going (2 from 3) but faces a sharp rise in competition level against seasoned handicappers in a big field.

runners_data.name: Wild Berries
runners_data.note: Hold-up fader who carries a headgear note (hg:p); five runs on similar going with no wins or places and a consistent pattern of finishing mid-division makes it hard to see where the improvement comes from here.

runners_data.name: Concaire
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a headgear note (hg:h) and a positive run when second over 7f on good ground; returns after 75 days and the drop back to 1m from that effort is a reasonable fit, though the big field could cause traffic issues from the rear.

runners_data.name: Giselles Defence
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature but the sheer volume of closers in this field means it will be shuffled into midfield rather than settled at the back where it operates best; the STYLE_FIT discount (0.91) applies and its recent form at shorter trips raises a distance concern at 1m.

runners_data.name: Virgil Tibbs
runners_data.note: True hold-up runner who will not get its preferred rearward position in this field; returns after 62 days and has been consistently mid-division without threatening on similar going (5 from 8 runs), with the style compromise making its task harder still.

runners_data.name: Dress Dance
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type that fades in the finish, held up at the back by preference but the crowded rear means it will be shuffled forward into mid-division; 106 days off the track is a significant fitness query and the form string shows no encouraging signs.

runners_data.name: Whosethebestboy
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up runner who fades late, dropping significantly in trip from its recent efforts over 12-13f; 107 days off and a headgear note (hg:h), and while it has decent form at the back of fields over longer distances, 1m on good ground in a 20-runner field is very different territory.

runners_data.name: Chou Chou
runners_data.note: Hold-up type by nature who won over 10f on good but is squeezed into midfield by the sheer number of closers; Colin Keane is the standout jockey booking in the field, which gives this horse a meaningful tactical advantage if a gap opens.

runners_data.name: Zephron
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a fading pattern and headgear (hg:b); all five recent runs on soft or heavy going rather than good, making this the most significant going concern in the race, and its natural hold-up style is compromised by the congested rear of the field.

runners_data.name: Cannonball Queen
runners_data.note: Hold-up fader with a headgear note (hg:p) and recent form showing consistent double-figure finishes; best effort was a fourth over 7f on good ground but Ben Coen cannot manufacture pace or position that isn't there in a horse running out of role.

runners_data.name: Duchess Anne
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up runner whose best recent results have been at 10f on good ground; Gary Carroll takes the ride and the headgear-free profile is cleaner than many rivals, though the step down to 1m and the crowded field make a prominent finish difficult to engineer.

runners_data.name: Spiritofthedawn
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning after 120 days, with headgear (hg:t) and only three career runs all on good-to-soft or soft; the going is quicker than anything it has experienced and the fitness question after a lengthy absence is significant.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire Myth
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with headgear (hg:b) and all recent form on Dundalk AW or soft going rather than good turf; the going switch is a real concern and returning after 82 days adds to the uncertainty, even if Nicola Burns's 5lb claim helps on weight.

runners_data.name: Marambo
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner returning just six days after its last outing; all five recent runs at this trip on good or AW have yielded poor finishing positions, though its natural pace means it will sit close to Land Of The Giants and give the field a consistent target to aim at.

runners_data.name: Plastic Paddy
runners_data.note: Fading hold-up type with headgear (hg:p) returning after 26 days; recent form over marathon distances is irrelevant here and the one 1m run shows a 14th-place finish, making this a very difficult assignment over a mile on good ground.

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse by nature whose recent form has been over 5-6f sprints, a significant style and trip mismatch for a 1m handicap; trained by Adrian McGuinness who is in form, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is among the highest in the race and the crowded rear compounds the positional problem.

races.paceDynamic: Land Of The Giants is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field and will set a controlled, uncontested pace on good ground over a flat Navan mile — there is no horse likely to seriously challenge for the lead, making this a genuinely tractable gallop rather than a contested burn-up. Marambo is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely settle just off the pace alongside Land Of The Giants, giving the field a small but defined lead group. The vast majority of the field are hold-up types by nature, but with so many genuine closers crowding the rear, horses such as Virgil Tibbs, Giselles Defence, I'm Spartacus, and Dress Dance are unlikely to secure their natural positions and will be shuffled into mid-division rather than resting at the tail of the field where they prefer. A steady, single-paced lead on good ground over one mile at Navan historically favours horses who can travel prominently or press from midfield at the two-furlong pole, as the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to set up a dramatic late burst for true back-of-the-field closers — the race shape therefore most benefits prominent racers and runners with a high cruising speed who can sit just off the leader and kick from a position of control.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Pressers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants sets a sustainable gallop and Marambo sits poised just off the lead, the race becomes a test of cruising speed rather than finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Land Of The Giants dictates from the front without pressure and Marambo tracks in second, with the pace honest but not fierce; at two furlongs out the race becomes a sprint from the front two with closers having too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slow enough to bunch the field and closers get a clear run through from midfield in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A compressed field means horses tracking in midfield-to-rear get a better tow into the race than their positioning suggests, and a strong finisher who times their run well could reel in a tiring front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate and a cluster of mid-division types advance together from three furlongs out, turning it into a cavalry charge.
scenarios.body: With so many redistributed hold-up horses filling the middle of the field, the race could become a mass move from midfield approaching the final turn, rewarding those with the best recent form and fitness.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants is given a completely unchallenged lead and quickens early in the straight before the field can organise a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: In a 20-runner field, closers can get boxed in or find traffic in the straight, allowing a front-runner on good ground to simply outstay a disorganised pursuit.

watchPoints.text: Land Of The Giants gets an uncontested lead — watch whether Adam Caffrey allows the gallop to become too slow in a 20-runner field, which would compress the field and invite a mass challenge in the straight.

Chou Chou has Colin Keane aboard — a jockey of this quality on a hold-up horse in a congested field could be the most important tactical factor if he finds a seam through traffic in the final two furlongs.

Dinamine has the strongest going record in the field (2W, 6P from 15 similar-going runs) and is fresh from a win 17 days ago — watch for Wesley Joyce to press forward from the rear as the pace settles in the back straight.

With at least 12 horses redistributed from their natural hold-up positions into the mid-division, the straight at Navan is likely to be extremely congested — horses drawn widest or with the clearest passage at the two-furlong pole will have a material advantage.

Zephron has no recent form on good ground (all five latest runs on soft or heavy) — if the going is riding on the quicker side of good, this horse's chance is materially weaker than its handicap mark suggests.

runners_data.name: Genuine Jim

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the ride for Donal Kinsella — a strong booking — and this genuine hold-up type is among those most likely to push forward given his natural speed; hg:tp worn, won over 8f on good and placed twice, 27 days since last run.|

runners_data.name: Thompson Gunner
runners_data.note: Colin Keane, the standout jockey booking of the race, rides this prominent-style horse with good-ground form (5/15 runs); beaten a nose at 8f on good here recently and Navan's flat mile suits his profile well — genuine danger.|

runners_data.name: Make The Tide
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for W McCreery, flagged for fading in finishes; trainer in form (5/13 T14) but the fade flag and 0W0P from three good-ground starts are cautionary, and 1m may stretch stamina.|

runners_data.name: Onyeisi

runners_data.name: Pettus Bridge
runners_data.note: Prominent-style fader for Denise Foster — shown a tendency to weaken late in all four career starts; 0W0P from four good-ground runs and an S (slipped up) last time, making him a significant risk even if he gets a good position.|

runners_data.name: Aghadrum Boy

runners_data.name: Pinball Wizard

runners_data.name: Winston's Promise

runners_data.name: Tariff

runners_data.name: Darwin's Angel
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for S M Duffy, naturally closes off the pace; 0W0P across 13 good-ground runs is a deeply uninspiring record and hg:p is worn, suggesting connections are searching for answers.|

runners_data.name: Borora Aura

runners_data.name: Hastily

runners_data.name: Bang Po

races.paceDynamic: Genuine Jim is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 20-runner flat mile handicap and, with no other natural lead horse to pressure him, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — a classic lone-leader scenario on good ground at Navan. Thompson Gunner, Borora Aura and Pettus Bridge are prominent types who will track close to the pace, but none are genuine pace-setters, so the fractions are unlikely to be truly searching. This field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses — Distillate, Aghadrum Boy, Micasso, Pinball Wizard, Chant d'Or, Winston's Promise, Tariff, Darwin's Angel, Hastily and Bang Po are all genuine closers who have been redistributed forward on the map simply because there are far more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; of these, Micasso (Seamie Heffernan) and Distillate are most likely to actually secure a forward position in running. A controlled pace set by Genuine Jim on good ground over one mile at Navan — a track that naturally rewards horses who travel well in midfield and produce a sustained finishing effort — means this race shape clearly favours prominent-to-midfield runners with genuine turn-of-foot, rather than true deep closers who will face a wall of horses if the pace never truly tests stamina.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Genuine Jim Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Genuine Jim sets a calm, uncontested lead and the pace is only moderate, allowing those tracking him to conserve energy for a sustained home-straight drive.
scenarios.body: Genuine Jim controls the fractions without challenge, keeping the race at a tempo that stretches the hold-up runners without burning off those just behind; Thompson Gunner and Micasso, positioned on or just off the leader, are ideally placed to pounce when the pace picks up in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Pair Steal
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace set by Genuine Jim is never meaningfully challenged and the field drifts in behind, allowing the leader and closest pursuers to steal a decisive advantage without being reeled in.
scenarios.body: A lack of urgency from the chasing pack — many of whom are out of their natural hold-up role and not travelling with authority — means the front two clear the field before the closers can organise; Genuine Jim and Thompson Gunner both benefit from the uncontested lead scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Surge, Late Rush Arrives
scenarios.trigger: If Thompson Gunner or Borora Aura raises the pace dramatically at halfway, turning this into a true test of stamina and opening the race up for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong gallop would stretch the field and give true closers like Moyassr or Concert Party legitimate late-run opportunities off a sound pace; however, with so many redistributed hold-up types not running from their natural position, the probability of a coordinated late challenge is meaningfully discounted.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Traffic, Outsider Slips Through
scenarios.trigger: If the large 20-runner field produces significant traffic issues and bunching in the straight, gifting a position-efficient horse an unimpeded run through gaps.
scenarios.body: In a 20-runner mile handicap on good ground, interference and crowding are a real risk, and a horse who finds clear daylight at the right moment could profit regardless of style; Borora Aura's consistent course form at Navan makes her the most likely beneficiary of a chaotic scenario.

watchPoints.text: Genuine Jim (sole front-runner, 76 days off) — watch his early sectionals closely; if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and dictates a modest pace, those immediately tracking him (Thompson Gunner, Micasso) become very dangerous.|

With 20 runners in a 1m handicap at Navan, severe traffic congestion in the straight is probable — watch that Colin Keane on Thompson Gunner secures a clean line early, as getting boxed behind the large field would be damaging for any prominent-style horse.|

Chant d'Or returns after 316 days absent — watch for any market move; if supported, it signals stable confidence, but the fade flag and short good-ground record mean an each-way interest would require very strong on-course evidence.|

Borora Aura runs just 6 days after her last outing — quick turnaround for a three-year-old; watch whether Michael Mulvany has freshened her enough, as her Navan course form (two placed runs on good) makes her a legitimate benchmark runner in this scenario.|

The Adrian McGuinness yard has two runners (Moyassr, Distillate) and is showing a 3/24 T14 stat — watch for any intra-stable support drift between the pair in the market as a guide to which the yard believes is better placed tactically.|

runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner for a yard with 5/13 in 14 days, but his record is 0W1P from eight good-ground attempts and he has been regressing (632605); at OR 74 carrying 134lbs, he is most likely to be a pacemaker who enhances the shape for others rather than lasting home himself.

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: In reality a true hold-up horse for Ms Sheila Lavery, but with the field stacked at the rear she is mapped to midfield where she will not be entirely comfortable; 0W4P from eleven good-ground starts and 55 days off are negatives, though her soft-ground placed efforts show she is capable of finishing into the frame when things fall right.

runners_data.name: Halon Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent Ben Coen ride who won over 7f on good ground and placed over 8f on soft; the 75-day absence is the primary concern, and his limited good-ground record (1W1P from four runs) leaves him lightly exposed for Ciaran Murphy's yard in this competitive field.

runners_data.name: Only One Scobie
runners_data.note: Tagged as a finisher who fades in the closing stages, which is a significant flag in a race guaranteed to be run at a strong pace; two wins at 8f suggest the trip is fine, but the fade pattern makes him vulnerable in a true end-to-end gallop even off the bottom weight in this age group.

runners_data.name: Felix Somary
runners_data.note: Prominent three-year-old for John S O'Donoghue who has placed three times at 8-10f on good ground; the visor (hg:v) indicates some quirk to manage and the recent form of 033 is encouraging without being exciting — likely to find a few too many at these weights.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for R P Cody's yard who has been displaced to midfield by the sheer weight of closing types in this field; his 0W1P good-ground record and inexperience at 3 years old mean even from a functional midfield position he must produce a clean run in a 21-runner race, which is far from guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Expound
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner tagged with tp headgear who is 1W4P from nine good-ground attempts but has been running over 10-16f and now drops sharply to a mile; the pace angle is clear but his stamina profile suggests he may be running to force the pace for stablemate connections rather than to win outright.

runners_data.name: Colpe Cross
runners_data.note: Unknown style runner returning from a 397-day absence for Miss Natalia Lupini with only three career runs, all on good ground over 10-12f; the step down in trip and extended layoff make her an extreme unknown quantity and she is almost impossible to assess with confidence in a race of this size and quality.

runners_data.name: Dream Legend
runners_data.note: A natural closer tagged with a finish-fade warning who has won twice on good ground over 8f; displaced from the rear to midfield by the overcrowded hold-up group, his best chance depends on finding a clear run in a 21-runner field from a position that is not his natural one — the style fit discount applies here.

races.paceDynamic: Exquisite Acclaim, Spodo Komodo, Great Mover, and Expound all want to be at the front, guaranteeing a strong, unrelenting gallop from the off over Navan's flat mile on good ground — stamina will be tested and there will be no easy time on the bridle early. The pace setters collectively create a race run genuinely end-to-end, which historically on this track and trip advantages horses who can sit just off the tempo and produce a sustained finish rather than a short, sharp closing burst. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all realistically secure their preferred positions, and among the leaders it is Exquisite Acclaim and Spodo Komodo who are most likely to actually control the rail and early order, with Great Mover and Expound likely pushed wider or slightly further back than ideal. Three genuine hold-up horses — Slight Of Foot, Anvika, and Dream Legend — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear will be more congested than usual in this 21-runner field, meaning their true closing runs may be compromised. This race shape, with its near-certain strong pace, heavily favours prominent-to-midfield runners with proven stamina at the trip who can travel comfortably in behind the leaders and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Exquisite Acclaim and Spodo Komodo force a genuine end-to-end gallop and the race is run at a relentless tempo from the outset.
scenarios.body: The strong pace burns off the true hold-up horses who lose their preferred closing ground, and a prominent racer travelling well in third or fourth position can pounce approaching the final furlong without expending energy in the scrimmage. Harana and Hygge both have the profile — prominent style, good-ground form, and effective at the mile trip — to exploit this shape ideally.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders burn each other out completely and the race slows enough in the middle furlong for a true hold-up horse to make ground.
scenarios.body: Marmeladova or No More Porter, sitting off a genuine pace that suddenly collapses entering the straight, could produce a sustained late run that catches a tiring front rank. However, with several hold-up types displaced from their natural position, the closing ground is crowded and the scenario is less clean than it appears on paper.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace setters engage in a war for supremacy early and the race becomes a test of attrition that opens the door for midfield runners with stamina.
scenarios.body: Zaraahmando has been consistently placed at this trip on good ground with a prominent-to-midfield style and would find this pace tempo highly suitable, while Morehampton showed ability over the mile on good ground in recent form. A genuine strong pace that doesn't fully collapse suits those who have the engine to grind past tiring rivals inside the final furlong rather than sprinting clear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Settles, Front Runner Lasts
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is not as severe as expected and one front-runner controls the tempo alone without being seriously pressured.
scenarios.body: Spodo Komodo or Exquisite Acclaim, if left alone to dictate from the front at a comfortable pace, could potentially see out the mile and hold on against a field compromised by congestion and horses racing out of role. This scenario requires the other pace horses to miss the break or be ridden with restraint, which given their profiles and connections is an unlikely but non-zero outcome.

watchPoints.text: Exquisite Acclaim and Spodo Komodo will fight for the lead from the break in a 21-runner field — watch for a fierce early duel that burns both out and sets up the race for prominent mid-pack horses like Harana and Zaraahmando.

Morehampton ran just two days ago (LR: 2d) and in a 21-runner mile handicap on the heels of a recent race, any residual fatigue could compromise his chance significantly despite promising ability figures.

Zaraahmando's trainer Andrew Slattery also rides the horse — a trainer-jockey combination in a wide-open 21-runner handicap can sometimes mean the market move is the only reliable signal; monitor the betting for unusual confidence before post time.

runners_data.name: Pampar Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist aged seven — the eldest in the field by some margin — with two placings on similar Good turf and a decent sim-going record, but a 33-day absence and a tendency to race from deep in large fields may leave her with too much ground to make up.|

runners_data.name: Queen Of Chenab
runners_data.note: Absent for 615 days, which is an enormous layoff concern; flagged as fading in finishes and her two sim-going runs returned no places, making it very hard to trust her for more than a market read.|

runners_data.name: Bang Bang
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form at 8-10f, but her natural instinct is to race from well off the pace — in a 23-runner field she is likely to find herself further back than ideal, and with STYLE_FIT of 0.92, her chance is tempered if the race doesn't produce a truly searching gallop.|

runners_data.name: Chosen One
runners_data.note: Has a solid placed effort at 10f on Good and races at her best when held up, though with several hold-up types in this field she will not get an unimpeded rail run; tongue-tie fitted and a 19-day turnaround keeps her fresh.|

runners_data.name: Estrallita
runners_data.note: Lightly raced, went 6th on Good over 8f as her only run; trainer Jack Davison has a quiet recent record and the unknown quantity tag makes her very speculative in a field this large.|

runners_data.name: Fairylike
runners_data.note: AP O'Brien's confirmed prominent runner, ridden by Wayne Lordan who is adept at positioning horses in large fields; her sole run produced a fourth at 10f on Good which is directly relevant, and she has every chance of tracking Mawhibah into an ideal pitch.|

runners_data.name: Gentle Soda
runners_data.note: Finished a distant 12th on debut at 8f on Good; naturally a hold-up type, flagged as fading in finishes, and at 15 days since that run is asked to step sharply up to 10f in a competitive maiden — the redistribution to map midfield reflects how unlikely she is to get a true front position.|

runners_data.name: Hey Stella
runners_data.note: Colin Keane steers a filly who has already placed third at 12f on Good at this course — the form is directly on-point for this race shape; lightly raced but the trip and going profile match well, and she is a key player in the prominent scenario.|

runners_data.name: Lamar Valley
runners_data.note: Two runs both produced well-beaten finishes at 8-10f on Good; the hold-up style and lack of any placed form makes her a very tough sell in a race of this quality and size.|

runners_data.name: Mawhibah
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, trained by Joseph O'Brien whose yard has strong recent form (T14: 12/79); off 18 days with solid form figures of 5-4-2 including two placings at this trip on Good, she holds the key tactical card here.|

runners_data.name: Near Perfection
runners_data.note: 130-day absence for Donnacha O'Brien — wears a tongue-tie and managed only fifth on debut at 12f on Good; the layoff and single run make her a significant unknown, though the yard's 3/17 recent trainer strike rate keeps her on the radar.|

runners_data.name: Orphanina
runners_data.note: Back after only 8 days, ran 9th and 10th in both outings at 8f on Good; hold-up style combined with a fading pattern and very modest form figures suggests she would need a career best.|

runners_data.name: Peshwari Nan
runners_data.note: Three runs all produced double-figure finishes; flagged as fading in finishes with Siobhan Rutledge aboard, and the 8-day turnaround after a tailed-off effort makes her very difficult to support.|

runners_data.name: Saxony Charms
runners_data.note: Three consistent fifths and a third on Good turf at 10f — a confirmed prominent runner who has been knocking on the door in a similar grade; blinkers fitted and Gary Carroll is an astute judge in large-field maidens.|

runners_data.name: Serendipia
runners_data.note: Has shown genuine consistency with two placed efforts in five Good-ground runs, all at 8-10f, and her natural hold-up style is a better fit for a more strongly-run race; tongue-tie worn, and W J Lee gives the yard an upgrade in the saddle.|

runners_data.name: Shanala
runners_data.note: Confirmed prominent runner dropping back in trip from 10f Good efforts; off 90 days for JP Murtagh, who has had a quiet recent yard record (T14: 1/32) — the layoff is the main query, but she should settle on the pace.|

runners_data.name: Socratea
runners_data.note: Ran seventh on debut at 8f Good; 70-day break for the McCreery yard and a hold-up style make her very hard to assess in a field this competitive — best treated as a market drifter watch.|

runners_data.name: Sunatia
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's confirmed prominent runner (T14: 2/20) ran a promising second at 9f Good on her latest start; Chris Hayes rides, the trip and going are ideal, and she is likely to track Mawhibah from a prime position.|

runners_data.name: Susie's Angel
runners_data.note: Apprentice Reese Holohan takes the ride on a filly who ran sixth at 7f Good on debut; jumping straight to 10f in a 23-runner field with the asking price of a claim apprentice is a significant challenge.|

runners_data.name: Ventriloquist
runners_data.note: 90-day absence and only run was an 11th in Soft, so the step to Good ground and a mile-and-a-quarter is a sizeable question mark; flags include fading in finishes and a John McConnell yard with moderate recent returns.|

runners_data.name: Vivere A Colori
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Mrs John Harrington (T14: 2/35 — solid stable in form); going unknown from a yard that produces well-readied debutants, and is the most interesting of the three first-time-out unknown quantities.|

runners_data.name: What Do You Say
runners_data.note: Second runner for A Oliver (alongside Saxony Charms) and a debut unknown; going profile unclassified and no historical form to anchor any assessment — purely speculative.|

runners_data.name: Windbourne
runners_data.note: Debutant for Patrick Foley who has no runners in the last 14 days (T14: 0/7); going unknown and entirely lightly raced — lowest-profile of the three debut unknowns in this field.|

races.paceDynamic: Mawhibah is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 23-runner fillies maiden over 1m2f at Navan on Good turf, and with no rival likely to genuinely press her for the lead, she is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. The three prominent types — Fairylike, Saxony Charms, and Shanala — will settle just behind her, creating an orderly head of affairs rather than a truly searching pace. With Mawhibah able to bowl along uncontested, the tempo is unlikely to be severe enough to burn off the hold-up brigade, but nor will it be slow enough to compress the race into a late sprint from deep. This shape — a single uncontested leader, modest early fractions, and a strung-out field in a large 23-runner field — marginally favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can travel close enough to pounce when the race quickens from two furlongs out, rather than genuine deep closers who will face traffic problems. The field carries far more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Gentle Soda, Serendipia, Bang Bang, and Chosen One are all natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map, and of those, the horses most likely to actually secure a forward position are Saxony Charms, Fairylike, and Sunatia given their confirmed prominent styles and more forward jockey profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mawhibah Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mawhibah is allowed to stride clear uncontested and the prominent trio settle within two lengths of her through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Mawhibah controls tempo throughout, the moderate pace keeps her fresh for a sustained run from two out, and those tracking her — Fairylike, Saxony Charms, Sunatia — are perfectly positioned to capitalise when the race unfolds.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mawhibah fades from the front in the final two furlongs and the first wave of prominent trackers overhaul her in a straightforward manner.
scenarios.body: The race sets up as a true test of staying power rather than a sprint finish, rewarding horses who raced keenly close to the pace without burning their engines in the early stages; Hey Stella's third on this course and trip is highly relevant here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Mawhibah sets a stronger gallop than expected or the prominent horses burn each other out, creating a gap for a well-positioned midfield runner to close.
scenarios.body: Serendipia's consistent placing record on Good turf at this trip profile suits a race that sets up slightly more end-to-end, and Chosen One's placed effort at 10f on Good also makes her one to monitor late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide in the straight in this large 23-runner heat and a lightly raced debutante or returning runner finds a clear run on the outside.
scenarios.body: Vivere A Colori, What Do You Say, or Windbourne — all debutants from capable yards — could exploit a messy finish if the pace conspires to leave a gap; Mrs John Harrington's runner Vivere A Colori carries the most stable-form credibility among the unknown quantities.

watchPoints.text: Mawhibah is the race-shaper — if she is allowed to control the tempo from the front without a challenger, horses tracking her (Fairylike, Saxony Charms, Sunatia) will be the primary dangers and any price move on them in running should be noted.

In a 23-runner field at Navan over 1m2f, traffic problems in the straight are a serious risk for the hold-up horses — Bang Bang, Serendipia, and Chosen One are all likely to need a lot of daylight that may not be available.

Queen Of Chenab returns after 615 days absent — any significant market support for a horse so long off the track in a filly's maiden should be treated as yard-confidence information and monitored carefully.

Hey Stella already placed third at this exact course and trip combination on Good ground — in a field full of unexposed types, that form line is unusually precise and Colin Keane's booking for G M Lyons is a positive pointer.

Three debutants (Vivere A Colori, What Do You Say, Windbourne) appear with no going classification — monitor market move at the off, as any of these from stronger yards could be well-prepared without public form to signal it.
